In Eur. (see p.vii) and Jpn. Ph. Eur. 6.2 (Trapidil). A white or almost white crystalline pow- der. Freely soluble in water; soluble in dehydrated alcohol and in dichloromethane. Protect from light. Profile Trapidil is a vasodilator and an inhibitor of platelet aggregation. It is also an antagonist of platelet-derived growth factor. It is used orally in the management of ischaemic heart disease in doses of 400 to 600 mg daily, in divided doses; doses of up to 600 mg daily may be used to prevent restenosis after angioplasty (but see below). Ischaemic heart disease is discussed under Atherosclero- sis (p.1159) and the treatment of its clinical manifestations is de- scribed under Angina Pectoris (p.1157) and Myocardial Infarc- tion (p.1175). ◊ References to anti-platelet activity. 1.
